welcome.title: Welcome to the QRA Parts Count Tool
welcome.body: This tour walks you through one complete parts count on a practice project: two PEFS sheets of an inlet separator, already imported. You will define the isolatable segment **IS-01**, count its leak sources and export the results. Nothing is saved to your computer, so try anything. It takes about 15 minutes.

openDrawing.title: Open a drawing
openDrawing.body: The drawing list on the left holds the project’s drawings. Click **PEFS-S-001 / 1** (sheet 1 of drawing PEFS-S-001) to open it. In your own projects, **+** above the list imports PDF, DWG and DXF files; you can also drop them onto the window.

navigate.title: Move round the sheet
navigate.body: Zoom with the mouse wheel, and pan by holding `Space` and dragging (or with the middle mouse button). `0` fits the whole page. The controls at the bottom of the sheet zoom, rotate and show the minimap.

findText.title: Find text on the drawing
findText.body: Press `Ctrl+F` (or the search button in the toolbar) and type **ESDV** to find the shutdown valves. `Enter` steps through the matches, and **Search all drawings** looks in every sheet. Press `Esc` to close the find bar when you are done.

createSegment.title: Create the segment IS-01
createSegment.body: An isolatable segment is the inventory between ESD valves. Click **+ Segment** in the left pane. Enter the label **IS-01**, the fluid **Gas / condensate**, pressure **45** and temperature **60**, then click **Create segment**. It becomes the active segment: new markers go to it.

esdv.title: Mark the first ESDV
esdv.body: Pick the **ESDV** tool in the toolbar (`E`) and click **ESDV-101** on the inlet line at the left of the sheet, inside the dashed ring (**Show me** zooms to it). The bar under the toolbar draws ESDVs as a ring or as a double line across the pipe.

esdvSegments.title: Set the segments on each side
esdvSegments.body: In the panel on the right, type the tag **ESDV-101** and set **Downstream segment** to **IS-01**: the flow comes from the wellhead manifold, outside the study, into IS-01. Leave **Upstream segment** as None. The panel says which segment counts the valve.

moreEsdvs.title: Mark the other ESDVs
moreEsdvs.body: Mark the other two ends of IS-01 the same way: **ESDV-102** on the gas line at the top right, and **ESDV-103** on the liquid line at the bottom right. For both, IS-01 is the **Upstream segment**: the flow leaves IS-01 through them.

endFlange.title: Mark an end flange
endFlange.body: The separator’s drain runs down to the closed drain, where IS-01 ends without an ESDV. Pick **End flange** (`F`), keep **Closed drain** in the bar, and click on the drain pipe just above **TO CLOSED DRAIN**. End flanges bound a segment but are not counted.

links.title: Link the off-page connectors
links.body: The gas line carries on on the next sheet. Open the **Project** menu and choose **Suggest drawing links…**: the app finds connector text that names another drawing. Click **Add**. (The **Drawing link** tool, `L`, draws a link by hand.)

autoTrace.title: Highlight the segment with Auto trace
autoTrace.body: Press `T`, or click **Auto trace** in the bar under the toolbar: the Highlighter paints IS-01’s pipework out to its ESDVs, the end flange and the off-page connector. Pipe it cannot place is shown dashed; click it to add it. `Ctrl+Z` undoes the whole trace.

dashed.title: Outline the separator
dashed.body: Equipment can be marked as an area too. Pick **Dashed highlight** (`D`) and drag a box round the separator **V-100**. Equipment placed on a segment’s highlighting or inside its zones goes to that segment, whichever segment is active.

followLink.title: Follow a drawing link
followLink.body: Pick **Select** (`V`) and click the **TO PEFS-S-002** connector at the top right: the link opens the sheet where the gas line continues. Then click **Back** at the top left of the sheet (or press `Alt+←`) to return.

startCount.title: Start the parts count
startCount.body: IS-01 is defined. Click **2 Parts count** in the header. A check lists anything that may be unfinished; click **Start counting**. While you count, the segment set-up is drawn faint and locked; **1 Segments** takes you back at any time.

equipmentBar.title: Choose what to count
equipmentBar.body: The toolbar now holds **Select**, **Circle** and **Stamp**, and the equipment bar under it chooses what the next circle counts. Click **Valve (manual)** in the bar.

circleValve.title: Count a valve
circleValve.body: Click the hand valve **HV-101** on the inlet line. The item editor on the right opens with the size field ready: type **8** and press `Enter`. You can add the tag **HV-101** in the editor too.

stamp.title: Count flanges with Stamp
stamp.body: Now the flanges either side of HV-101. Choose **Flange** in the equipment bar (under **… more** if the bar is short of room), click **F-1**, type **8** and press `Enter`. Then pick **Stamp** (`S`) and click **F-2**: Stamp repeats the last item without opening the editor.

findSimilar.title: Find similar symbols
findSimilar.body: Let the app find the other valves. Pick **Select** (`V`), click the HV-101 circle, then **Find similar symbols** in the right pane. Step through the violet rings: **Accept** the valves of IS-01 (HV-102, HV-104 and HV-105) and **Reject** HV-103, which is beyond ESDV-102.

sizes.title: Check the sizes
sizes.body: Accepted valves take the example’s size, 8". Press `0` to see the whole sheet, then click each one and correct its size in the item editor: **HV-102** is 6", **HV-104** is 4" and **HV-105** is 2". `Shift`+click selects several markers, to edit them together.

countTable.title: Read the count table
countTable.body: The **count table** on the right totals IS-01 by equipment type, actuation and size bin as you click. Click a count in it to highlight the markers behind it on the drawing.

finishCount.title: Finish the count
finishCount.body: Count the rest on your own: choose the type in the equipment bar before you click, or press its key just after. The instrument taps **PT-101** (¾") and **LT-101** (1") are small-bore connections (`3`), **V-100** a pressure vessel (`4`) and **P-101** a pump (`5`); **NRV-101** is a 4" check valve and **F-3** a 6" flange. Markers missing a type or size get an amber outline.

note.title: Add a note for the checker
note.body: Notes record assumptions and open points. In **Notes** at the bottom right, type a note such as **V-100 counted as one pressure vessel** and press `Ctrl+Enter`. Set your initials in **Settings** to sign your notes.

status.title: Mark the segment as counted
status.body: At the top of the right pane, set IS-01’s **Status** to **Counted**, and enter your initials in **Counted by**. The segment list shows each segment’s status.

export.title: Check and export
export.body: Click **Export** at the top right. The pre-export check lists anything unfinished, with **Show** to go to it. Keep **Excel workbook** and **Annotated drawings (PDF)** ticked and click **Export** (or **Export anyway**). In the practice project, **Download exports (.zip)** keeps the files.

finish.title: You have done a parts count
finish.body: Segment defined, parts counted, a note for the checker and the results exported. For a real study, start a **New project** in an empty folder, adjust the equipment library to the client’s dataset, and map the client’s Excel template once in **Project › Template mapper**. Press `F1` at any time for the documentation.
